What is Ibernia in one sentence?: What is Ibernia in one sentence?
Ibernia ia a goal-based financial planni: Ibernia ia a goal-based financial planning app for advisors that models cashflows, savings pots, and what-ifs, then generates draft advice with firm specific rules
Use this section to add your client’s ke: Use this section to add your client’s key life events and financial goals. These events shape the cashflow forecast and can be linked to specific transactions such as incomes or expenses. Add new events to the timeline or move existing ones to adjust their timing.
Enter all savings pots, pensions, and in: Enter all savings pots, pensions, and investment accounts held by your client in this section (excluding property). In the event of an income shortfall, these pots will be drawn down in the sequence displayed below. You may rearrange the order by dragging and dropping the pots, or by using the up/down arrows.
These are the default assumptions used t: These are the default assumptions used to save time when creating a new plan. You can change them anytime for each client.
The assumed rate inflation is expected t: The assumed rate inflation is expected to rise by, per year. This assumption affects the entire cashflow model, as future values are inflation adjusted into real terms.
How satisfied are you with your current: How satisfied are you with your current financial planning?
Input all regular and one-off income sou: Input all regular and one-off income sources and expenses relevant to your client. These entries will feed directly into the cashflow model, influencing the projected financial outcomes. You may link transactions to specific events, and adjust timing or frequency as needed.
Add all expected contributions to and wi: Add all expected contributions to and withdrawals from your client’s savings pots throughout the forecast period. Contributions will transfer funds from the client’s Current account to a selected Savings Pot. Withdrawals will move funds from a Savings Pot back to the Current account to cover shortfalls.

LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.HERO: A healthy cash buffer is usually between 3 and 12 months of expenses
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.RANGE_ARIA: Months of expenses your cash could cover, shown against zones below three months, three to twelve months, and above twelve months
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.DIAG_HIGH: Higher than you may need in cash
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.COPY_LOW: That may be a thin buffer for unexpected costs or a temporary loss of income.
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.COPY_OK: That sits in a range many people use for short term flexibility and emergencies.
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.COPY_HIGH: That is more than many people typically keep for short term needs.
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.COPY_NEUTRAL: Add your monthly expenses to see how many months of spending your cash could cover.
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.PRACTICAL: Keeping some cash helps with emergencies and flexibility, but holding much more than you may need can reduce long term growth.
LEARN_CASH_BUFFER.NUANCE: The right buffer depends on income stability, dependants, debt, health, and how comfortable you are with risk.
LEARN_INFLATION.TITLE: Inflation
LEARN_INFLATION.SUBTITLE: See how the value of money changes over time
LEARN_INFLATION.HERO: Inflation means prices rise over time. When prices go up, the same money buys less.
LEARN_INFLATION.SUPPORTING_COPY: The number in your account can stay the same, but its purchasing power falls over time.
LEARN_INFLATION.EXPLANATION: The number in your account stays the same. What you can buy does not. Inflation reduces purchasing power over time.
LEARN_INFLATION.CAUSES_INTRO: Inflation can be classified into three types:
LEARN_INFLATION.CAUSE_DEMAND_DESC: When popular concert tickets sell out quickly, their resale value soars, illustrating how strong consumer demand can drive prices up.
LEARN_INFLATION.CAUSE_COST_DESC: Rising global oil prices directly increase shipping and manufacturing costs, forcing businesses to raise prices for consumers.
LEARN_INFLATION.CAUSE_BUILTIN_DESC: As workers demand higher wages to keep up with living costs, businesses pass these increased labor costs onto consumers through higher prices.
LEARN_INFLATION.COUNTRIES_TITLE: How Different Can Inflation Be Across Countries?
LEARN_INFLATION.COUNTRIES_INTRO: Inflation changes over time and across borders. Some economies experience higher or more volatile inflation than others.
LEARN_INFLATION.COUNTRIES_FOOTNOTE: EU uses HICP. Japan, the United States and China use CPI. These measures are highly useful for comparison, but they are not perfectly identical.
LEARN_COMPOUND.HERO_TITLE: Compound interest makes money grow on growth
LEARN_COMPOUND.HERO_SUBTITLE: Even small differences in return can compound into a much bigger outcome over the years
LEARN_COMPOUND.CONTEXT_HINT: We start from the cash in your savings pots—adjust the numbers anytime to explore different scenarios.
LEARN_COMPOUND.SUMMARY_CLOSER: Even with the same starting amount, small differences in return and time can lead to very different outcomes. The earlier you start, the more compounding can work for you.
LEARN_COMPOUND.SUPPORTING_COPY: Your money can grow. But when returns are reinvested, growth starts generating more growth. That is what makes compound interest so powerful over time.
LEARN_COMPOUND.INFLATION_NOTE: Inflation still matters, which is why real value should grow faster than prices.
LEARN_COMPOUND.SIMPLE_VS_COMPOUND_BTN: Difference between simple and compound interest
LEARN_COMPOUND.COMPARE_TITLE: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
LEARN_COMPOUND.COMPARE_INSIGHT: With simple interest, returns only grow on the original amount. With compound interest, returns also grow on past returns.
LEARN_COMPOUND.COMPARE_SUBTITLE: Same money. Same rate. The key difference is whether returns are reinvested.
LEARN_COMPOUND.CARD_COMPOUND_LINE2: Returns are reinvested and start earning returns too.
LEARN_COMPOUND.CARD_GAP_LINE1: The longer time passes, the bigger the difference becomes.
LEARN_COMPOUND.COMPARE_TAGLINE: The longer you stay invested, the bigger the gap can get.
LEARN_COST_WAITING.HERO_TITLE: Delaying an investment can cost more than it seems
LEARN_COST_WAITING.SUPPORTING_COPY: The longer money stays uninvested, the less time it has to compound. That difference can become significant over many years.
LEARN_COST_WAITING.SUMMARY_EMPTY: Enter an amount to see how different waiting periods compare.

welcomeModal.title: Welcome to Ibernia
welcomeModal.bodyPrimary: This view was built for you by {{advisorBold}} to help you see your financial life in one place: how your finances may evolve over time, where your wealth stands today, and how protected you are against the unexpected.
welcomeModal.bodyDisclaimer: The future cannot be foreseen, so everything shown is an approximation based on today's information and a set of assumptions. Treat it as a planning tool, not a prediction. Review it with {{advisorBold}} and keep it updated as life changes.
